findings.title: Timeout can leave later flusher processes running
findings.body: When the join deadline expires while waiting for one process, this `break` skips every remaining process, including the `terminate()` call for those processes. They can continue flushing Redis segments and producing to Kafka after the strategy has shut down. Ensure every process is stopped even when the deadline is exhausted.

findings.title: Inserting this parameter breaks positional callers
findings.body: `produce_to_pipe` was previously the third positional argument to `SpanFlusher`; inserting `max_processes` before it means existing calls such as `SpanFlusher(buffer, next_step, callback)` now treat the callback as a process limit. Initialization then attempts to use that callback in `min()` and fails. Preserve the existing positional argument order, for example by adding the new parameter after `produce_to_pipe`.

findings.title: A negative process limit silently disables all flushers
findings.body: The `--flusher-processes` option accepts negative integers, and a negative `max_processes` makes `num_processes` negative. The subsequent `range(self.num_processes)` creates no worker processes, so segments are never flushed to Kafka and can accumulate in Redis. Reject non-positive limits or otherwise ensure at least one worker is created.
